Keywords:                                                    Drawing on existing market designs with independent resource participation in electricity markets, this study
Wholesale electricity markets                                analyzes participation models for hybrid resources combining renewable generation and storage. Two models
Production cost model                                        are considered: in the ﬁrst, the components operate independently, with the Independent System Operator (ISO)
Hybrid energy resource
                                                             managing the storage state of charge (SoC); in the second, the hybrid resource acts as an integrated unit, submit-
Energy storage
                                                             ting oﬀers as a “black box” and managing its SoC internally. Using a production cost model for the zonal New York
                                                             Bulk Power System, we evaluate trade-oﬀs in system reliability, market eﬃciency, and asset proﬁtability. Our
                                                             results provide several key insights for policymakers, showing that the ISO-managed granular model enhances
                                                             social welfare through explicit SoC management, while the simpler integrated model is more computationally
                                                             eﬃcient, but may cause more real-time violations and lower overall proﬁts.

network representation, realistic supply-demand mixes, or increasing
VER penetration. As a result, its ﬁndings cannot be readily generalized
to large-scale power systems for deriving regulatory insights.

                                                                                                   Market operations typically involve both a real-time unit commit-
                                                                                               ment (RTSCUC) and a real-time economic dispatch (RTSCED) model.
                                                                                               However, for the purposes of this study, a simpliﬁed real-time market
                                                                                               structure is implemented using a single unit commitment and dispatch
                                                                                               model with a one-hour optimization horizon and one-hour time resolu-
                                                                                               tion. This model enables the commitment of quick start resources and
                                                                                               the re-dispatch of already committed units to address real-time imbal-
                                                                                               ances.
